ITEM 10
                               FINANCING

         You are required to purchase all of your Robots and Robot Doors only from our Coralview
    Affiliate.

         You may purchase your initial inventory of Robots and Robot Doors outright, or if you qualify,
   you may elect to purchase the Robots and the Robot Doors over time, in which case you will sign the
    then-current Equipment Supply Sale and Security Agreement (Equipment Agreement,) the most recent
    version of which is attached at Exhibit 8 to the Franchise Agreement.

            Further, if you financed the initial inventory and if qualified at the time of the proposed additional
    purchase, you may finance future equipment needs under the same Equipment Agreement; understanding,
   however, that certain financial terms will vary.

               If you did not finance your initial purchase of equipment, you still can apply to our Coralview
    Affiliate to purchase future equipment needs by signing the then-current Equipment Agreement, the terms
    of which may be significantly different from those found in Exhibit 8. There is no guaranty that you will
   be able to finance additional equipment, as our Coralview Affiliate will make that determination at the
    time you apply, using such standards as it is then using to qualify any other franchisee.

         The terms of the financing as September 10, 2018 are stated below.

    the purchase price is $925 for each RC 306 Robot, is $1,300 for each RS 612 Robot, and is $150 for each

      Our Coralview Affiliate reserves the right to change the manufacturer of, the model of and the
price and shipping costs of the Robots and the Robot Doors at any time and in any amount. Once we
learn of any such increase, we will provide you no less than 60 days written notice before the new model
is introduced or the new price comes into effect. You will not be required to purchase new equipment if
new models of Robots are adopted, but if you seek to purchase additional Robots, or at the time you
receive Successor Franchise Rights or at the time that you are permitted to transfer the Equipment
Agreement, you may be required to purchase new Robots and Robot Doors.

         2.    You will pay the then-current minimum Robot Purchase Deposit for the Initial Robot
Package that is financed. The current Robot Purchase Deposit is $150 for each RC 306 Robot and each
RS 612 Robot (for a total of $1,800 for the Initial Robot Package,) and $50 for each Robot Door.  If you
are able to finance the entire remaining amount of Robots, Coralview will finance approximately between
83% if the RC 306 Robots are financed and 88% if the RS 612 Robots are financed.  If the doors are
financed, Coralview could finance approximately 66%.  If our Coralview Affiliate determines that your
credit history requires it, they may charge more of a down payment for some or all of the Robots and
Robot Doors, which amount could equal up to 40% of the entire amount to be financed.  There is no
formula for determining under what circumstances an adjustment to the down payment will occur, and as
a result, we cannot state such circumstances here.

         3.      Currently, the “amount financed” will be the total of the Robot Purchase Price and
shipping and handling costs.

      As of September 10, 2018, Franchisees located in: AK, CO, CT, DE, IA, IL, IN, KS, KY, MA,
MI, MD, ME, MN, MO, ND NE, NH, NJ, NY, OH, OK, PA, RI, SD, TN, UT, VT, WI, WV and WY, are
in the “Northern Markets,” the season of which runs from April 1 through October 31 (the “Northern
Season;) and Franchisees located in all other states (but Alaska) are located in the “Southern Market,” the
season of which runs from March 1 through October 31 (the “Southern Season”).

      The number of payment that a franchisee will make in any year is based upon the Market in
which he or she is located. For the year in which the franchisee signed the Equipment Agreement, he or
she will make payments for each week remaining in the Season in which the Franchised Location is
found.  For instance,  if a franchisee in Colorado signs the Equipment Agreement on March 1, the
Northern Season will not yet have begun, and he or she will start making payments weekly beginning
with April 1 and through the end of the Northern Season.  If the franchisee signed on June 1, he or she
will pay for the weeks of the Northern Season that follow. After that season has ended, no payments will
be due until the beginning of the new Northern Season. The interest not paid during the “off-season” is
added to the principal and is paid off by extending the number of weeks for which payments are made.
For instance, if the payment calculated at the time the Equipment Agreement is signed is $132 per week,
that will remain the same for the entire life of the loan. The interest during the off season will accrue, and
then beginning with the payments for the next Season, so much of the $132 per week payment will be
used as is necessary to pay off the accrued interest for the past off season.

       For the initial purchase of equipment, the amount financed will be based upon the number of
Robots that are financed, then-current interest rate and the shipping and insurance costs. The amount
financed will be disclosed to you (including the annual percentage rate (APR) - which is a statement of

===== PAGE 27 =====
the annual interest-rate plus the Finance Charges expressed on a annual basis), before you sign the then-
current Equipment Agreement. The APR will vary with each purchase based on the Principal that is to be
financed, the then-current annual interest rate and shipping and handling costs and as a result, it cannot be
quoted here for any particular loan. As of September 10, 2018 however, and assuming that 12 RS 612
Robots at $1,250 per Robot are purchased in Texas, at 10.3% per annum and shipping and handling of
$480 and with a total of approximately 169 weekly payments, (but subtracting from this amount the
$1,800 Purchase Deposit Fee that is paid up front,) the APR will be approximately 10.3%. Making the
same assumptions but for the purchase for 12 RC 306 Robots at $925 each, the APR will also be 10.3%.

       For any future purchases of equipment, the amount financed, the interest rate, the then-current
Finance Charges, and the terms of such financing, plus the disclosure of the APR will be disclosed before
you sign the then-current Equipment Agreement.

         4.     Though all franchisees will pay the same interest rate regardless of being in the Northern
or Southern Market, the number of weekly payments and the final payoff figure will vary depending on:
(i) the amount financed; (ii) the interest rate set at the time you sign the Equipment Agreement; (iii) the
date of the purchase, and (iv) your location in the country.  Interest will continue to accrue during the off
season for franchisees in either the Norther Market or Southern Market.

          If the Robots are purchased on a day other than the first day of a week, and if the week in which
the Franchisee signs is during the Northern Season or Southern Season, then the payment for that week
will be prorated based on the number of days remaining in such week.

       There is no pre-payment penalty.

         5.      All Franchisees will pay the same then-current interest rate, which as of June 20, 2018 is
approximately 10.3%. per annum (Interest Rate.) The Interest rate is currently calculated based upon the
interest rate quoted by the London Interbank Offered Rate (“LIBOR” - which is the benchmark interest
rate that banks use to charge other banks for some loans) which was approximately 2.8% (as printed in
the Wall Street Journal on September 10, 2018) plus 7.5%. Your initial interest rate will be quoted to you
before you sign the then-current Equipment Agreement.

      The Interest Rate will vary for the purchase of any additional Robots or Robot Doors under the
same Equipment Agreement, will vary for the purchase of equipment on any new Equipment Agreement
signed, and may also vary at the time that you assign the Equipment Agreement to another franchisee
(after first receiving our Coralview Affiliate’s express written permission to do so.) We will inform you
of our Coralview Affiliate’s change to the Interest Rate at the time that you apply for new financing or at
the time you seek to assign your Equipment Agreement. Once the Interest Rate has been determined, it
will be fixed for the term of Equipment Agreement to which it applies.

      The total number of months that it takes to payoff the purchase will also vary depending on the
factors stated above, but it is approximately between 40 and 44 months from the date that the Equipment
Agreement is signed.

         6.     The Equipment Agreement is also a security agreement that serves as a pledge of the
equipment financed. To perfect such pledge, you will sign a “financing statement,” “UCC-1”, or similar
security device that will be filed in the records of the county or state in which you operate.  If you are a
business entity other than a sole proprietorship, your equity owners will each sign a personal guaranty in
favor of our Coralview Affiliate.  If the business-entity franchisee breaches the terms of the Equipment
Agreement, then in addition to any other remedies available, it also has the right to collect any amount
due from each guarantor.

        the Franchise Agreement; and (ii) a default under other agreements with us or our related companies.

       demand, presentment for payment, notice of nonpayment and protest, and notice of amendments or
        modifications.  You also waive any defense under the statute of limitations and allow that a
        confessed judgment may be taken against you. (See Exhibits D-1, D-2 and D-3.)

financing.  The review will include a financial analysis, assessment of the use and understanding of our
programs, and your adherence to the requirements under the Franchise Agreement.

program, we or RSG may receive payments from such lender. As of the issuance date of this disclosure
document, RSG does not receive payment from lenders. See Item 8.

===== PAGE 25 =====
ITEM 10

                                    FINANCING


 We may offer, directly or indirectly, financing for a portion of the Initial Franchise Fee, generally,
 no more than one half of the Initial Franchise Fee. Before agreeing to finance any of the Initial
 Franchise Fee, we reserve the right to qualify you according to a number of factors, including but
 not limited to, creditworthiness. We reserve the right to refuse financing to you, even if you qualify,
 at our sole discretion. We do not guarantee your Vehicle lease(s) or other obligations.

 Promissory Notes

 If you desire to finance a portion of your Initial Franchise Fee, and such financing is available, and
 you qualify, you must complete Exhibit J, “Promissory Note.” The terms of the Promissory Note
 may vary with respect to amount financed, the due date and the monthly payments. Our standard
 Promissory Note provides that the principal balance of the note is to be repaid in 36 monthly
 installments at the annual interest rate of 10%. Your interest rate, loan term and down payment
 amounts may change according to current promotional programs. We reserve the right to change
 the offered interest rate, loan term and down payment amounts at any time after written notice to
 you. We require a personal guarantee to be signed by you and by all the principals of your business
 as we deem necessary for adequate security (See Section 25, Franchise Agreement and Guaranty
 Agreement). If you do not pay the installments due on the promissory note on time, we can require
 you to pay the entire debt and all accrued interest and late charges on demand, terminate your
 Franchise Agreement, and/or require you to pay for our court costs and attorneys’ fees if we have
 to institute a collection action against you. (See Exhibit  J, Promissory Note) and Franchise
 Agreement, Section 22.3, 23.2).

 Guaranty Agreement

 We require all of our franchisees to personally guarantee that any and all amounts due and owing
 to us will be paid in accordance with the terms disclosed in our Franchise Agreement, as we deem
 necessary for adequate security.  If you are not an individual, all principals of your organization
  (i.e., persons or partners who sign the Franchise Agreement and in the case of a corporation,
 partnership, or limited liability company, the shareholders, partners, managers or members of that
 organization), must sign the Guaranty Agreement presented at the end of the Franchise Agreement
 as Exhibit C-6, as we deem necessary for adequate security. This is a personal guarantee of the
 obligations under the Franchise Agreement. This Guaranty Agreement gives us the right to collect
 any amounts due us from you personally. Neither we, nor our affiliates, guarantee any notes, leases
 or other obligations you may have with a third party.

 Waiver of Defenses

 You waive presentment, protest and notice, and the benefit of the homestead exemption, and
 further agree to pay reasonable attorneys’ fees and all court costs should it become necessary to
 place the Promissory Note in the hands of an attorney for collection or to protect our interests as
 provided in the Promissory Note (See Promissory Note). The Franchise Agreement contains a
 provision in which you waive all questions of personal jurisdiction or venue, that is, any claim that
 the court in which the action is brought is inconvenient or inappropriate, and your right to a jury
 trial (See Franchise Agreement, Sections 30.2 and 30.6). Generally, you have the right to a jury trial
 in civil litigation. The laws of certain states do not permit you to waive your right to a jury trial.
25

===== PAGE 26 =====
Except as disclosed in this Item 10, we do not offer financing that requires you to waive notice or
 waive a defense against us.

 Other Financing Information

 We have not yet nor do we presently intend to transfer, assign, discount, or sell to a third party any
 Promissory Note, any portion of a Promissory Note or other payment obligation executed by any
 franchisee. However, we reserve the right to do so in the future under terms that we have not yet
 determined. We will determine the terms of any assignment. If we do decide to sell or assign any
 Promissory Note or portion thereof or any other payment obligation executed by any franchisee,
 that franchisee may lose all its defenses against us as a result of the sale or assignment.

 We do not receive direct or indirect payments for placing financing. If you do not finance through
 us, or if you do not qualify under our financing program, we may recommend that you contact
 certain lenders who may be able to offer you financing. If you finance through a third party, it may
 request you to personally guarantee the loan, and if you do not make timely payments, it may be
 able to accelerate your loan, confess judgment on your loan, remove your equipment, and/or
 charge you liquidated damages. We do not receive any compensation or fee from any third party
 lender. We do not guarantee your obligations to third parties.

  DIVERSITY AND VETERAN INCENTIVE PROGRAM

       We  participate  in the  International Franchise Association’s Veteran’s Transition Franchise
    Initiative (known as VetFran®). We are currently offering a diversity and veteran incentive program to

   Econo Lodge Disclosure Document – April 1, 2018            36

===== PAGE 42 =====
encourage and increase the diversity of our franchise system and the hospitality industry as well as to
encourage entrepreneurs that have served in the United States military and been honorably discharged
from service (“Diversity and Veteran Incentive”).  The Diversity and Veteran Incentive Program is
intended to attract top hotel developers from diverse backgrounds and involves our commitment of capital
to incentivize qualifying franchisees to develop either a newly constructed Choice-branded hotel or
convert an existing hotel to a Choice-branded hotel.  Qualifying franchisees who enter into franchise
agreements to re-license Choice branded hotels that are currently part of the Choice franchise system are
not eligible to receive a Diversity and Veteran Incentive; however these franchisees will be given a 50%
discount on the then-current affiliation fee due in connection with the re-licensed franchise agreement
(see below).

        Qualifications

      To qualify for the Diversity and Veteran Incentive Program, you must meet all of the following
conditions: you must request the Diversity and Veteran Incentive at the time of application; you must
meet our then-current qualifications for new franchisees (including our standard credit review); you must
own the hotel; if you are an individual, you must identify to us the characteristics and background that
will contribute to the diversity of our franchise system and the hospitality industry or if you are veteran
you must demonstrate that you have served in the United States military and have been honorably
discharged from service; or if you are a legal entity, you must be at least 51% legally and beneficially
owned by persons that can demonstrate to us characteristics and background that will contribute to the
diversity of our franchise system and the hospitality industry or meet the requirements of a veteran stated
above.  The Diversity and Veteran Incentive Program may not be combined with any other incentive
program that we may be offering at the time of your application and we may discontinue the Diversity
and Veteran Incentive Program at any time.

       Incentive

       Each Diversity and Veteran Incentive we make for a hotel using the ECONO LODGE Marks will
be for $750 per room in the hotel (maximum of $50,000). Each incentive will be evidenced by a 10-year
forgivable promissory note (see Exhibit I) (the “Note”). We will pay the proceeds of the Note to you only
after the Opening Date of your hotel. You may use the proceeds of the Note for any purpose related to
the hotel. We do not require collateral for this Note, but may require personal guaranties. Forgiveness of
the Note will be amortized over 10 years (beginning on the Opening Date of your hotel) using a straight-
line method, so that the Note will be completely forgiven if you do not commit certain defaults under the
Note beginning upon signing of the franchise agreement and ending 10 years after the Opening Date. The
Note is structured to provide for one payment at the end of 10 years; however, you do not have to make
payments on the Note if you remain in good standing under your franchise agreement.  If you default in
the obligations of your franchise agreement, your franchise agreement is terminated or expires, you die or
you file for bankruptcy, then the entire remaining unforgiven principal balance is immediately due along

ITEM 10

                              FINANCING

 AFFILIATION FEE PROMISSORY NOTE

          In our sole discretion and on approval of your credit, we may offer to finance the affiliation fee
  without interest. In that event, you must sign a promissory note (see Exhibit H). Note payment is due in
  one full lump sum generally within three months after the note is signed. The note may be accelerated upon
  default and provides for a waiver of presentment, demand for payment, notice of dishonor, protest, and
  includes a confession of judgment clause. Personal guarantees may be required. The note contains no pre-
  payment penalty.

 DIVERSITY AND VETERAN INCENTIVE PROGRAM

      We  participate  in the  International Franchise Association’s Veteran’s Transition Franchise
  Initiative (known as VetFran®). We are currently offering a diversity and veteran incentive program to
  encourage and increase the diversity of our franchise system and the hospitality industry as well as to
  encourage entrepreneurs that have served in the United States military and been honorably discharged from
  service (“Diversity and Veteran Incentive”). The Diversity and Veteran Incentive Program is intended to
  attract top hotel developers from diverse backgrounds and involves our commitment of capital to
  incentivize qualifying franchisees to develop either a newly constructed Choice-branded hotel or convert

                                           43
  Rodeway Franchise Disclosure Document-April 1, 20187, as amended October 1, 2017

===== PAGE 49 =====
an existing hotel to a Choice-branded hotel. Qualifying franchisees who enter into franchise agreements to
re-license Choice branded hotels that are currently part of the Choice franchise system are not eligible to
receive a Diversity and Veteran Incentive; however these franchisees will be given a 50% discount on the
then-current affiliation fee due in connection with the re-licensed franchise agreement (see below).

        Qualifications

      To qualify for the Diversity and Veteran Incentive Program, you must meet all of the following
conditions: you must request the Diversity and Veteran Incentive at the time of application; you must meet
our then-current qualifications for new franchisees (including our standard credit review); you must own
the hotel; if you are an individual, you must identify to us the characteristics and background that will
contribute to the diversity of our franchise system and the hospitality industry or if you are veteran you
must demonstrate that you have served in the United States military and have been honorably discharged
from service; or if you are a legal entity, you must be at least 51% legally and beneficially owned by persons
that can demonstrate to us characteristics and background that will contribute to the diversity of our
franchise system and the hospitality industry or meet the requirements of a veteran stated above. The
Diversity and Veteran Incentive Program may not be combined with any other incentive program that we
may be offering at the time of your application and we may discontinue the Diversity and Veteran Incentive
Program at any time.

       Incentive

       Each Diversity and Veteran Incentive we make for a hotel using the RODEWAY Marks will be for
$750 per room in the hotel (maximum of $50,000). Each incentive will be evidenced by a 10-year forgivable
promissory note (see Exhibit I) (the “Note”). We will pay the proceeds of the Note to you only after the
Opening Date of your hotel. You may use the proceeds of the Note for any purpose related to the hotel.
We do not require collateral for this Note, but may require personal guaranties. Forgiveness of the Note
will be amortized over 10 years (beginning on the Opening Date of your hotel) using a straight-line method,
so that the Note will be completely forgiven if you do not commit certain defaults under the Note beginning
upon signing of the franchise agreement and ending 10 years after the Opening Date. The Note is structured
to provide for one payment at the end of 10 years; however, you do not have to make payments on the Note
if you remain in good standing under your franchise agreement. If you default in the obligations of franchise
agreement, your franchise agreement is terminated or expires, you die or you file for bankruptcy, then the
entire remaining unforgiven principal balance is immediately due along with interest (accruing on the
remaining unforgiven balance only) from the original date of the Note at an interest rate of prime plus 2%.
The maximum interest rate in California is 10% annually. Under the Note, you must waive demand,
presentment for payment, protest, notice of dishonor and your right to a jury trial. On your default, you
also must pay all reasonable expenses, costs and attorneys’ fees that we incur in collecting the Note. The
Note contains no pre-payment penalty.

          If you qualify for a Diversity and Veteran Incentive, you may request amortization over 5 years
instead (beginning on the Opening Date of your hotel) using a straight-line method, so that the Note will
be completely forgiven if you do not commit certain defaults under your franchise agreement upon signing
of the franchise agreement and ending 5 years after the Opening Date.  If you request a 5 year Note, the
incentive will be 50% of the amount of the 10 year Note, and will be limited to a maximum of $25,000.
Each incentive will be evidenced by a 5 year Note in the same form attached as Exhibit I. The Note is
structured to provide for one payment at the end of 5 years; however, you do not have to make payments
on the Note if you remain in good standing under your franchise agreement. If you default in the obligations
of your franchise agreement, your franchise agreement is terminated or expires, you die or you file for
bankruptcy, then the entire remaining unforgiven principal balance is immediately due along with interest
(accruing on the remaining unforgiven balance only) from the original date of the Note at an interest rate


                                         44
Rodeway Franchise Disclosure Document-April 1, 20187, as amended October 1, 2017

===== PAGE 50 =====
of prime plus 2%. The maximum interest rate in California is 10% annually. Under the Note, you must
waive demand, presentment for payment, protest, notice of dishonor and your right to a jury trial. On your
default, you also must pay all reasonable expenses, costs and attorneys’ fees that we incur in collecting the
Note. The Note contains no pre-payment penalty.

       Termination Rights

        In addition, unless you have signed a 5 year promissory note, you and we must agree to waive our
right to terminate the franchise agreement, without cause, on the 5th anniversary of the Opening Date.

DIVERSITY AND VETERAN RE-LICENSING INCENTIVE

          If you: 1) qualify for the Diversity and Veteran Incentive Program; and 2) purchase a hotel that is
a RODEWAY branded hotel operating as part of the Choice franchise system at the time of purchase; and
3) enter into a franchise agreement with Choice to re-license the hotel as a RODEWAY branded hotel, you
will be granted a 50% discount on the then-current affiliation fee due in connection with your franchise
agreement. Franchisees that enter into franchise agreements with Choice for the re-licensing of an existing
Choice brand hotel and qualify and accept the Diversity and Veteran Incentive are not eligible to participate
in any other incentive program.

PMC COMMERCIAL TRUST

     We have entered into a non-exclusive Qualified Vendor agreement with a third party named PMC
Commercial Trust (previously known as PMC Capital, Inc.) (“PMC”), which is a company authorized to
provide loans. Under this agreement, PMC may offer conventional and Small Business Administration
(“SBA”) financing to those of our franchisees that qualify and choose to use PMC to finance some of the
following costs: affiliation fee, site acquisition, construction or remodeling, equipment and/or fixtures,
opening inventory or supplies, ongoing inventory or supplies, replacement of equipment or fixtures, and
other continuing expenses. These loans are generally for up to 70% to 85% of the value of the collateral
and range from $500,000 to $5,000,000 for acquisitions, refinances and construction/permanent loans.

         Interest rates are generally variable and are at PMC’s discretion. You are not required to use PMC
as your lender. If you choose to use PMC as your lender, you must enter into agreements with PMC,
substantially in the form attached as Exhibit J or as PMC may otherwise require depending on your specific
loan. The loan will be for up to 25 years and will require monthly payments, with the amount of the
payments based on the terms agreed upon. You must grant a first lien on land and building, a first lien on
furniture, fixtures and equipment and, if necessary, a lien on your personal assets. PMC will require that
you personally guarantee the loan. The loans can be pre-paid but there may be a pre-payment penalty.

          If you default on the note, the entire remaining principal balance becomes due and the lender may
have the right to take possession of the collateral and/or sell or lease the collateral. You must waive your
rights to presentment for payment, demand, protest, notice of non-payment or dishonor, notices of protest
and all other demands or notices. On default, the note will bear interest at the maximum rate permitted by
applicable law. You must also pay PMC all the costs of collection or costs of exercising its remedies,
including attorneys’ fees. You must waive your right to object to jurisdiction in the courts of Dallas, Texas
as the venue for the resolution of disputes and must waive your right to a trial by jury. See the sample
documents in Exhibit J for PMC’s additional rights and remedies.

        In consideration of Choice’s agreement to grant PMC access to our marketing channels, Choice
will receive from PMC a flat payment annually.


                                         45
Rodeway Franchise Disclosure Document-April 1, 20187, as amended October 1, 2017

===== PAGE 51 =====
DIRECT CAPITAL, A DIVISION OF CIT BANK, N.A.

     We have entered into a non-exclusive Qualified Vendor agreement with a third party named Direct
Capital, A CIT Company (“DC”) under which DC may offer conventional and lease financing to those of
our franchisees that qualify and choose to use DC to finance some of the following costs: affiliation fee,
costs  to meet brand  standards,  property improvement  or remodeling, equipment  and/or  fixtures,
replacement of equipment or fixtures, and other continuing expenses. These loans are generally for up to
100% of the value of the collateral and range from up to $250,000 without financial review and up to
$20,000,000 or more with full financial review.

         Interest rates are fixed and are determined at DC’s discretion in accordance with its standard
underwriting practices. You are not required to use DC as your lender.  If you choose to use DC as your
lender, you must enter into one or more agreements with DC, substantially in the form attached as Exhibit
J or as DC may otherwise require depending on your specific loan. The loan will be for 12 to 84 months
and will require monthly payments, with the amount of the payments based on the terms agreed upon. You
must grant a first lien on the financed equipment and, if applicable, a security interest and lien on the land
or building. DC may require that you personally guarantee the loan. The loans can be pre-paid and there
is no pre-payment penalty.

          If you default on the loan, the entire remaining balance becomes due and DC may have the right to
take possession of the collateral and/or sell or lease the collateral.  You must waive your rights to
presentment for payment, demand, protest, notice of non-payment or dishonor, notices of protest and all
other demands or notices. On default, the loan will bear interest at the rate set forth in the loan agreement.
You must also pay DC all the costs of collection or costs of exercising its remedies, including attorneys’
fees. You must waive your right to object to jurisdiction in the courts of Rockingham County, NH as the
venue for the resolution of disputes and must waive your right to a trial by jury. See the sample documents
in Exhibit J for DC’s additional rights and remedies.

        In consideration of Choice’s agreement to grant DC access to our marketing channels, Choice will
receive from DC a flat payment annually.

BALBOA CAPITAL CORPORATION

     We have entered into a non-exclusive Qualified Vendor agreement with a third party named Balboa
Capital Corporation (“Balboa”), which is a company authorized to provide loans. Under this agreement,
Balboa may offer conventional and lease financing to those of our franchisees that qualify and choose to

 AFFILIATION FEE PROMISSORY NOTE

          In our sole discretion and on approval of your credit, we may offer to finance the affiliation fee
  without interest. In that event, you must sign a promissory note (see Exhibit H). Note payment is due in
  one full lump sum generally within three months after the note is signed. The note may be accelerated upon
  default and provides for a waiver of presentment, demand for payment, notice of dishonor, protest, and

 DIVERSITY AND VETERAN INCENTIVE PROGRAM

      We  participate  in the  International Franchise Association’s Veteran’s Transition Franchise
  Initiative (known as VetFran®). We are currently offering a diversity and veteran incentive program to
  encourage and increase the diversity of our franchise system and the hospitality industry as well as to
  encourage entrepreneurs that have served in the United States military and been honorably discharged from
  service (“Diversity and Veteran Incentive”). The Diversity and Veteran Incentive Program is intended to
  attract top hotel developers from diverse backgrounds and involves our commitment of capital to
  incentivize qualifying franchisees to develop either a newly constructed Choice-branded hotel or convert

                                           35

an existing hotel to a Choice-branded hotel. Qualifying franchisees who enter into franchise agreements to
re-license Choice branded hotels that are currently part of the Choice franchise system are not eligible to
receive a Diversity and Veteran Incentive; however these franchisees will be given a 50% discount on the
then-current affiliation fee due in connection with the re-licensed franchise agreement (see below).

        Qualifications

      To qualify for the Diversity and Veteran Incentive Program, you must meet all of the following
conditions: you must request the Diversity and Veteran Incentive at the time of application; you must meet
our then-current qualifications for new franchisees (including our standard credit review); you must own
the hotel; if you are an individual, you must identify to us the characteristics and background that will
contribute to the diversity of our franchise system and the hospitality industry or if you are veteran you
must demonstrate that you have served in the United States military and have been honorably discharged
from service; or if you are a legal entity, you must be at least 51% legally and beneficially owned by persons
that can demonstrate to us characteristics and background that will contribute to the diversity of our
franchise system and the hospitality industry or meet the requirements of a veteran stated above. The
Diversity and Veteran Incentive Program may not be combined with any other incentive program that we
may be offering at the time of your application and we may discontinue the Diversity and Veteran Incentive
Program at any time.

       Incentive

       Each Diversity and Veteran Incentive we make for a hotel using the RODEWAY Marks will be for
$750 per room in the hotel (maximum of $50,000). Each incentive will be evidenced by a 10-year forgivable
promissory note (see Exhibit I) (the “Note”). We will pay the proceeds of the Note to you only after the
Opening Date of your hotel. You may use the proceeds of the Note for any purpose related to the hotel.
We do not require collateral for this Note, but may require personal guaranties. Forgiveness of the Note
will be amortized over 10 years (beginning on the Opening Date of your hotel) using a straight-line method,
so that the Note will be completely forgiven if you do not commit certain defaults under the Note beginning
upon signing of the franchise agreement and ending 10 years after the Opening Date. The Note is structured
to provide for one payment at the end of 10 years; however, you do not have to make payments on the Note
if you remain in good standing under your franchise agreement. If you default in the obligations of franchise
agreement, your franchise agreement is terminated or expires, you die or you file for bankruptcy, then the
entire remaining unforgiven principal balance is immediately due along with interest (accruing on the
remaining unforgiven balance only) from the original date of the Note at an interest rate of prime plus 2%.
The maximum interest rate in California is 10% annually. Under the Note, you must waive demand,
presentment for payment, protest, notice of dishonor and your right to a jury trial. On your default, you
also must pay all reasonable expenses, costs and attorneys’ fees that we incur in collecting the Note. The
Note contains no pre-payment penalty.

          If you qualify for a Diversity and Veteran Incentive, you may request amortization over 5 years
instead (beginning on the Opening Date of your hotel) using a straight-line method, so that the Note will
be completely forgiven if you do not commit certain defaults under your franchise agreement upon signing
of the franchise agreement and ending 5 years after the Opening Date.  If you request a 5 year Note, the
incentive will be 50% of the amount of the 10 year Note, and will be limited to a maximum of $25,000.
Each incentive will be evidenced by a 5 year Note in the same form attached as Exhibit I. The Note is
structured to provide for one payment at the end of 5 years; however, you do not have to make payments
on the Note if you remain in good standing under your franchise agreement. If you default in the obligations
of your franchise agreement, your franchise agreement is terminated or expires, you die or you file for
bankruptcy, then the entire remaining unforgiven principal balance is immediately due along with interest
(accruing on the remaining unforgiven balance only) from the original date of the Note at an interest rate

equipment or fixtures, and other continuing expenses. LIVE OAK BANK also offers construction and
development financing to Franchisees.

      LIVE OAK BANK offers several loan products to hotel operators; therefore, loan term, structure,
down payment, and rate all depend on factors including but not limited to: loan use, loan size, and
applicant’s credit application. Loan amounts range from $50,000 - $15,000,000, typical down payments
range from 0 - 15%, terms from 10-25 years (with shorter terms available upon occasion), and rates from
Prime + 1.25% to Prime + 4.5%.  Interest rates are typically adjustable tied to the prime rate (as noted in
the wall street journal) or sometimes fixed and are determined at LIVE OAK BANK’s discretion in
accordance with its standard underwriting practices. You are not required to use LIVE OAK BANK as
your lender.

          If you choose to use LIVE OAK BANK as your lender, you must enter into one or more agreements
with LIVE OAK BANK, substantially in the form attached as Exhibit J or as LIVE OAK BANK may
otherwise require depending on your specific loan. Loan structure and terms are typically decided during
the underwriting process and is dependent on the use of loan funds, and the loan product.  Typical loan
structure requires a first lien on all furniture, fixtures, and equipment being financed with loan proceeds, as
well as a best available lien on your business assets. Based on the loan structure and use of funds, a security
interest and  lien on the land or building  will be a requirement of development or construction
financing. LIVE OAK BANK will require a personal guarantee of all owners owning 20% or more of the
applicant business. Loans with a term of 15 years or less carry no pre-payment penalties, with loans of
greater length carrying a 3 year prepayment penalty (5%, 3%, 1%).

        In consideration of Choice’s agreement to grant LIVE OAK BANK access to our marketing
channels, Choice will receive from LIVE OAK BANK a flat payment annually.

NORTHEAST BANK, which  is a company authorized  to provide  loans. Under  this agreement,
NORTHEAST BANK may offer conventional and Small Business Administration (SBA) financing to those
of our franchisees that qualify and choose to use NORTHEAST BANK to finance some of the following
costs: affiliation fee, costs to meet brand standards, property improvements or remodeling, equipment
and/or  fixtures, replacement of equipment or  fixtures, debt refinancing, and other reasonable and
permissible uses of business debt allowed by the SBA or NORTHEAST BANK’s commercial lending
policies. These loans are generally available for up to 90% of the value of the collateral and range from
$350,000 to $10,000,000.

underwriting practices. You are not required to use NORTHEAST BANK as your lender.  If you choose

intended to attract top hotel developers from diverse backgrounds and involves our commitment of capital
to incentivize qualifying franchisees to develop either a newly constructed Choice-branded hotel or
convert an existing hotel to a Choice-branded hotel.  Qualifying franchisees who enter into franchise
agreements to re-license Choice branded hotels that are currently part of the Choice franchise system are

        Qualifications

      To qualify for the Diversity and Veteran Incentive Program, you must meet all of the following
conditions: you must request the Diversity and Veteran Incentive at the time of application; you must
meet our then-current qualifications for new franchisees (including our standard credit review); you must
own the hotel; if you are an individual, you must identify to us the characteristics and background that
will contribute to the diversity of our franchise system and the hospitality industry or if you are veteran
you must demonstrate that you have served in the United States military and have been honorably
discharged from service; or if you are a legal entity, you must be at least 51% legally and beneficially
owned by persons that can demonstrate to us characteristics and background that will contribute to the
diversity of our franchise system and the hospitality industry or meet the requirements of a veteran stated
above.  The Diversity and Veteran Incentive Program may not be combined with any other incentive
program that we may be offering at the time of your application and we may discontinue the Diversity
and Veteran Incentive Program at any time.

       Incentive

       Each Diversity and Veteran Incentive we make for a hotel using a QUALITY Mark listed in Item
13 will be for $1,500 per room in the hotel (maximum of $125,000). Each incentive will be evidenced by
a 10-year forgivable promissory note (see Exhibit I) (the “Note”). We will pay the proceeds of the Note
to you only after the Opening Date of your hotel. You may use the proceeds of the Note for any purpose
related to the hotel. We do not require collateral for this Note, but may require personal guaranties.
Forgiveness of the Note will be amortized over 10 years (beginning on the Opening Date of your hotel)
using a straight-line method, so that the Note will be completely forgiven if you do not commit certain
defaults under the Note beginning upon signing of the franchise agreement and ending 10 years after the
Opening Date. The Note is structured to provide for one payment at the end of 10 years; however, you do
not have to make payments on the Note if you remain in good standing under your franchise agreement.
If you default in the obligations of your franchise agreement, your franchise agreement is terminated or
expires, you die or you file for bankruptcy, then the entire remaining unforgiven principal balance is
immediately due along with interest (accruing on the remaining unforgiven balance only) from the
original date of the Note at an interest rate of prime plus 2%. The maximum interest rate in California is
10% annually. Under the Note, you must waive demand, presentment for payment, protest, notice of
dishonor and your right to a jury trial. On your default, you also must pay all reasonable expenses, costs
and attorneys’ fees that we incur in collecting the Note. The Note contains no pre-payment penalty.

          If you qualify for a Diversity and Veteran Incentive, you may request amortization over 5 years
instead (beginning on the Opening Date of your hotel) using a straight-line method, so that the Note will
be completely forgiven if you do not commit certain defaults under your franchise agreement beginning
upon signing of the franchise agreement and ending 5 years after the Opening Date.  If you request a 5
year Note, the incentive will be 50% of the amount of the 10 year Note, and will be limited to a maximum
of $62,500. Each incentive will be evidenced by a 5 year Note in the same form attached as Exhibit I.
The Note is structured to provide for one payment at the end of 5 years; however, you do not have to
make payments on the Note if you remain in good standing under your franchise agreement.   If you
default in the obligations of your franchise agreement, your franchise agreement is terminated or expires,
you die or you file for bankruptcy, then the entire remaining unforgiven principal balance is immediately
due along with interest (accruing on the remaining unforgiven balance only) from the original date of the
Note at an interest rate of prime plus 2%. The maximum interest rate in California is 10% annually.

Because the financed amount is a fee owed to the franchisor, the economic architecture is seller credit/deferred receivable exposure (Score 2), not funded cash credit. versions.codingNote: The franchisor extends seller credit by allowing a franchisee to pay up to 50% of the initial franchise fee over time via a promissory note and installment payments. ITEM 10

          If you are purchasing a franchise for an Existing Center or a MatchMaker Center, you may elect to
pay the initial marketing fee in two installments, as follows: $7,000 when you sign the Franchise Agreement
and the balance of $7,000 within 90 days of when you sign the Franchise Agreement. If you elect to pay
the initial marketing fee in two installments, you will sign our form secured promissory note (the “Note”)
(attached to this Disclosure Document as Exhibit K). The second installment is due and payable in one
lump sum. The principal amount due under the Note may be prepaid without penalty.

     No interest is due under the Note except in the event of default or a transfer of the Note, in which
case the outstanding principal amount will be immediately due and payable and interest will accrue at the
lesser of 18% per year or the highest contract rate of interest allowed by law. Any default under either the
Franchise Agreement or the Note is deemed a default under both the Franchise Agreement and the Note
and we may pursue remedies available to us under both the Franchise Agreement and the Note. If we are
required to take any action to enforce payment of the Note, you will be required to pay all costs, fees and
expenses (including attorneys’ fees) we incur to enforce our rights under the Note. The Note provides for a
waiver of  diligence, presentment and demand for payment,  protest,  notice, notice of protest and
nonpayment, dishonor and notice of dishonor.

      The amount due under the Note is secured by the Franchise Agreement, and each owner who signs
a Guaranty and Assumption of Obligations will be required to sign the Note acknowledging that his or her
obligations under the Guaranty and Assumption of Obligations extend to the Note.

           It is not our practice or intent to sell, assign or discount to a third party all or part of the Note, nor
do we receive any consideration for placing the Note with a lender.

       Other than the above, we do not offer direct or indirect financing or guarantee your note, lease or
other obligations.

operating a new group, as applicable. All remaining payments are due by the 15th of each month in

includes a promissory note with a personal guaranty, and a security agreement securing the assets of your
business. We have the right to require you to establish a bank sweep, draft or other similar type of
electronic funds transfer account in which you must deposit the required monthly payment, which account
we may automatically access for any payment due to us. You are allowed to prepay at any time without
penalty. No interest will be charged unless you are late on a payment. If you are late in paying your fees, a
$50 per day late fee and a monthly interest late charge equal to the maximum rate permitted under the

ITEM 10

                             FINANCING

AFFILIATION FEE PROMISSORY NOTE

        In our sole discretion and on approval of your credit, we may offer to finance the affiliation fee
without interest.  In that event, you must sign a promissory note (see Exhibit I). Note payment is due in
one full lump sum generally within three months after the note is signed. The note may be accelerated
upon default and provides for a waiver of presentment, demand for payment, notice of dishonor, protest,
and includes a confession of judgment clause. Personal guaranties may be required. The note contains no
pre-payment penalty.

DIVERSITY AND VETERAN INCENTIVE PROGRAM

     We  participate  in the  International Franchise Association’s Veteran’s Transition Franchise
Initiative (known as VetFran®). We are currently offering a diversity and veteran incentive program to
encourage and increase the diversity of our franchise system and the hospitality industry as well as to
encourage entrepreneurs that have served in the United States military and been honorably discharged
from service (“Diversity and Veteran Incentive”).  The Diversity and Veteran Incentive Program is
intended to attract top hotel developers from diverse backgrounds and involves our commitment of capital
to incentivize qualifying franchisees to develop either a newly constructed Choice-branded hotel or
convert an existing hotel to a Choice-branded hotel.  Qualifying franchisees who enter into franchise
agreements to re-license Choice branded hotels that are currently part of the Choice franchise system are
not eligible to receive a Diversity and Veteran Incentive; however these franchisees will be given a 50%
discount on the then-current affiliation fee due in connection with the re-licensed franchise agreement
(see below).

        Qualifications

      To qualify for the Diversity and Veteran Incentive Program, you must meet all of the following
conditions: you must request the Diversity and Veteran Incentive at the time of application; you must
meet our then-current qualifications for new franchisees (including our standard credit review); you must
own the hotel; if you are an individual, you must identify to us the characteristics and background that
will contribute to the diversity of our franchise system and the hospitality industry or if you are veteran
you must demonstrate that you have served in the United States military and have been honorably
discharged from service; or if you are a legal entity, you must be at least 51% legally and beneficially
owned by persons that can demonstrate to us characteristics and background that will contribute to the
diversity of our franchise system and the hospitality industry or meet the requirements of a veteran stated
above.  The Diversity and Veteran Incentive Program may not be combined with any other incentive
program that we may be offering at the time of your application and we may discontinue the Diversity
and Veteran Incentive Program at any time.

       Incentive

       Each Diversity and Veteran Incentive we make for a hotel using the MAINSTAY SUITES Marks
will be for $1,500 per room in the hotel (maximum of $125,000). Each incentive will be evidenced by a
10-year forgivable promissory note (see Exhibit J) (the “Note”). We will pay the proceeds of the Note to
you only after the Opening Date of your hotel. You may use the proceeds of the Note for any purpose
related to the hotel. We do not require collateral for this Note, but may require personal guaranties.
Forgiveness of the Note will be amortized over 10 years (beginning on the Opening Date of your hotel)


MainStay Franchise Disclosure Document-April 1, 2018
                                          40

===== PAGE 46 =====
using a straight-line method, so that the Note will be completely forgiven if you do not commit certain
defaults under the Note beginning upon signing of the franchise agreement and ending 10 years after the
Opening Date. The Note is structured to provide for one payment at the end of 10 years; however, you do
not have to make payments on the Note if you remain in good standing under your franchise agreement.
If you default in the obligations of your franchise agreement, your franchise agreement is terminated or
expires, you die or you file for bankruptcy, then the entire remaining unforgiven principal balance is
immediately due along with interest (accruing on the remaining unforgiven balance only) from the
original date of the Note at an interest rate of prime plus 2%. The maximum interest rate in California is
10% annually. Under the Note, you must waive demand, presentment for payment, protest, notice of
dishonor and your right to a jury trial. On your default, you also must pay all reasonable expenses, costs
and attorneys’ fees that we incur in collecting the Note. The Note contains no pre-payment penalty.

          If you qualify for a Diversity and Veteran Incentive, you may request amortization over 5 years
instead (beginning on the Opening Date of your hotel) using a straight-line method, so that the Note will
be completely forgiven if you do not commit certain defaults under your franchise agreement beginning
upon signing of the franchise agreement and ending 5 years after the Opening Date.  If you request a 5
year Note, the incentive will be 50% of the amount of the 10 year Note, but will be limited to a maximum
of $62,500. Each incentive will be evidenced by a 5 year Note in the same form attached as Exhibit J.
The Note is structured to provide for one payment at the end of 5 years; however, you do not have to
make payments on the Note if you remain in good standing under your franchise agreement.   If you
default in payments due to us under your franchise agreement, your franchise agreement is terminated,
you sell the hotel, you die or you file for bankruptcy, then the entire remaining unforgiven principal
balance is immediately due along with interest (accruing on the remaining unforgiven balance only) from
the original date of the Note at an interest rate of prime plus 2%. The maximum interest rate in California
is 10% annually. Under the 5 year Note, you must waive demand, presentment for payment, protest,
notice of dishonor and your right to a jury trial. On your default, you also must pay all reasonable
expenses, costs and attorneys’ fees that we incur in collecting the Note.  The Note contains no pre-
payment penalty.

       Termination Rights

        In addition, unless you have signed a 5 year promissory note, you and we must agree to waive our
right to terminate the franchise agreement, without cause, on the 5th anniversary of the Opening Date.

DIVERSITY AND VETERAN RE-LICENSING INCENTIVE

          If you: (1) qualify for the Diversity and Veteran Incentive Program; and (2) purchase a hotel that
is a Choice branded hotel operating as part of the Choice franchise system at the time of purchase; and (3)
enter into a franchise agreement with Choice to re-license the hotel as a Choice branded hotel, you will be
granted a 50% discount on the then-current  affiliation fee due in connection with your franchise
agreement.  Franchisees that enter into franchise agreements with Choice for the re-licensing of an
existing Choice brand hotel and qualify and accept the Diversity and Veteran Incentive are not eligible to
participate in any other incentive program.

PMC COMMERCIAL TRUST

     We have entered into a non-exclusive Qualified Vendor agreement with a third party named PMC
Commercial Trust (previously known as PMC Capital, Inc.) (“PMC”), which is a company authorized to
provide loans. Under this agreement, PMC may offer conventional and Small Business Administration
(“SBA”) financing to those of our franchisees that qualify and choose to use PMC to finance some of the
following costs: affiliation fee, site acquisition, construction or remodeling, equipment and/or fixtures,


MainStay Franchise Disclosure Document-April 1, 2018
                                          41

===== PAGE 47 =====
opening inventory or supplies, ongoing inventory or supplies, replacement of equipment or fixtures, and
other continuing expenses. These loans are generally for up to 70% to 85% of the value of the collateral
and range from $500,000 to $5,000,000 for acquisitions, refinances and construction/permanent loans.

         Interest rates are generally variable and are at PMC’s discretion. You are not required to use
PMC as your lender. If you choose to use PMC as your lender, you must enter into agreements with
PMC, substantially in the form attached as Exhibit J or as PMC may otherwise require depending on your
specific loan. The loan will be for up to 25 years and will require monthly payments, with the amount of
the payments based on the terms agreed upon. You must grant a first lien on land and building, a first lien
on furniture, fixtures and equipment and, if necessary, a lien on your personal assets. PMC will require
that you personally guarantee the loan. The loans can be pre-paid but there may be a pre-payment penalty.

          If you default on the note, the entire remaining principal balance becomes due and the lender may
have the right to take possession of the collateral and/or sell or lease the collateral. You must waive your
rights to presentment for payment, demand, protest, notice of non-payment or dishonor, notices of protest
and all other demands or notices. On default, the note will bear interest at the maximum rate permitted by
applicable law. You must also pay PMC all the costs of collection or costs of exercising its remedies,
including attorneys’ fees. You must waive your right to object to jurisdiction in the courts of Dallas,
Texas as the venue for the resolution of disputes and must waive your right to a trial by jury. See the
sample documents in Exhibit J for PMC’s additional rights and remedies.

        In consideration of Choice’s agreement to grant PMC access to our marketing channels, Choice
will receive from PMC a flat payment annually.

BALBOA CAPITAL CORPORATION

Balboa Capital Corporation (“Balboa”), which is a company authorized to provide loans. Under this
agreement, Balboa may offer conventional and lease financing to those of our franchisees that qualify and
choose to use Balboa to finance some of the following costs: affiliation fee, costs to meet brand standards,
property improvement or remodeling, equipment and/or fixtures, replacement of equipment or fixtures,
and other continuing expenses. These loans are generally available for up to 100% of the value of the
collateral and generally range from $5,000 to $1,000,000.

         Interest rates are fixed and are determined at Balboa’s discretion in accordance with its standard
underwriting practices. You are not required to use Balboa as your lender.  If you choose to use Balboa
as your lender, you must enter into one or more agreements with Balboa, substantially in the form
attached as Exhibit J or as Balboa may otherwise require depending on your  specific financing
agreement. The financing agreement will be for between 24 to 84 months and will require monthly or
quarterly installment payments, with the amount of the payments based on the terms agreed upon. You
must grant a first lien on the financed equipment and, if applicable, a security interest and lien on the land
or building. Balboa may require that you personally guarantee the financing agreement. The financing
agreement can be pre-paid and there is no pre-payment penalty.

          If you default on the financing agreement, the entire remaining balance becomes due and Balboa
may have the right to take possession of the collateral and/or sell or lease the collateral. You must waive
your rights to presentment for payment, demand, protest, notice of non-payment or dishonor, notices of
protest and all other demands or notices. On default, the loan will bear interest at the rate set forth in the
loan agreement. You must also pay Balboa all the costs of collection or costs of exercising its remedies,
including attorneys’ fees. You must waive your right to object to jurisdiction in the courts of California

as the venue for the resolution of disputes and must waive your right to a trial by jury. See the sample
documents in Exhibit J for Balboa’s additional rights and remedies.

        In consideration of Choice’s agreement to grant Balboa access to our marketing channels, Choice
will receive from Balboa a flat payment annually.

ACCESS POINT FINANCIAL

     We have entered into a non-exclusive Qualified Vendor agreement with a third party named
ACCESS POINT FINANCIAL (“APF”), which is a company authorized to provide loans. Under this

ITEM 10   FINANCING

There are two fees for which we may offer to finance a portion; the initial franchise fee and the
account acquisition fee. We reserve the right to refuse do offer you financing if we believe, in our
sole judgment, that extension of the financing would constitute an unsound business decision.
Within one week of providing us with all of the information we require, we will provide you
with a determination of whether or not we will extend financing to you. We do not engage in the
practice of selling, assigning, or discounting to a third party, in whole or in part, any note,
contract or other instrument executed by you.  However, we reserve the right to do so in the
future.

Financing of the Initial Franchise Fee.

We may offer to finance a portion of your initial franchise fee. If financed, the amount of the
initial franchise fee ranges from $2,700 to $47,000 depending on the franchise plan you choose.
You are responsible for providing a down payment in cash or certified funds upon signing the
Franchise Agreement. The amount of the down payment ranges between $1,000 and $39,500
depending on the size of the franchise plan you have selected.  Also upon signing the initial
franchise agreement you will sign a promissory note for the remainder of the initial franchise fee
due to us.  If you are a partnership, limited liability company or corporation, then the note must
be guaranteed individually by all of the partners, members or shareholders, as applicable. Please
see Item 5 of this Disclosure Document for more information pertaining to the initial franchise
fee and the amounts involved for each franchise plan.

The promissory note  is payable over a three-year period in equal monthly installments and
accrues interest per year on the unpaid principal amount at the lower of ten percent (10%) or the
maximum rate allowed by applicable law.  You may pre-pay the note at any time without
penalty. In the event of nonpayment or other default under the promissory note or in the event of
a breach of the Franchise Agreement, the payment of the principal may be accelerated at our
option without notice or demand to you. You also will be responsible for our attorney's fees as
well as your own, in the event you are in default. Upon transfer, expiration or termination of the
franchise, any principal balance becomes immediately payable. The form of promissory note is
attached to this Disclosure Document as Exhibit B.

Financing of the Account Acquisition Fee.

In the event you choose to accept additional customer accounts offered by us, we may offer to
finance all or a portion of your account acquisition fee.  Please see Item 6 of this Disclosure
Document for an explanation of how the account acquisition fee is calculated. The Account

for paying the account acquisition fee: the sweat equity option or the loan option.

If the sweat equity option is elected and approved by us, then a certain amount will be deducted
from your monthly statement in consecutive, equal monthly installments  until the account
acquisition fee has been paid in full. No interest is assessed with this option.

If the loan option is elected and approved by us, then you will owe us the original acquisition fee
less the amount of any down payment you may have made on the fee. The balance is payable
over a 12-month period in equal monthly installments and aecrues interest at ten percent (10%)
per year on the unpaid principal or the maximum rate allowed by applicable law. We will be
allowed to deduct your monthly payment from your accumulated total gross billings. If you do
not make a payment, then the missed payment can be deducted in full from your next monthly
statement. If there are performanee cancellations, if you abandon a customer account, if you
breach the Franchise Agreement or our Policy and Procedures Guide or if we believe that your
ability to repay the debt  is impaired or unsatisfactory, then we are entitled to call the debt
immediately due and payable without any notice. You also will be responsible for our attorney's
fees as well as your own, in the event you are in default.

You may pre-pay the debt at any time without penalty. Upon transfer, expiration or termination
of the franchise, any principal balance becomes immediately payable.
